transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-05-04
Start: 15:00 PT
Duration: 48m
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ethan Park (SE), Jonas Reed (CSM); Sara Lopez, Raj Patel, Emily Tan, Noah Rivers, Hannah Chu (Finova)

Auto-generated Summary: quick intake for payments-focused pilot, security + procurement alignment.

00:00:02 Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for making time. quick round robin, we have Maya and Ethan from Redwood, Jonas on for CS.
00:00:10 Sara Lopez: Hi, Sara here. Appreciate it. We're trying to figure out vendor pathing for an inference partner for auth flows.
00:00:18 Raj Patel: Raj - security. main thing for us is PCI scope and data residency, and we need to understand whether card data ever leaves our control.
00:00:26 Ethan Park: Yep, understood. quick framing — Redwood offers hosted, dedicated reserved capacity, and private (VPC/on-prem) variants. For PCI heavy flows, many customers go with private or dedicated with tokenization in-place.
00:00:38 Noah Rivers: When you say private, do you mean full on-prem? or VPC peering? our ops team prefers not to have PANs in any vendor S3.
00:00:47 Ethan Park: Both. private is an option where the control plane can be customer-managed and you run an on-prem package or a VPC-deployed stack. with VPC peering and customer KMS, Redwood won't retain plaintext - default is no persistent storage of raw inputs unless you enable logs.
00:01:03 Hannah Chu: what about telemetry and traces? we need to keep forensic logs for 18 months for payments investigations.
00:01:10 Maya Chen: we provide audit logs and trace hooks; retention can be configured as part of an enterprise add-on, but we should scope retention and cost with legal.
00:01:20 Emily Tan: from a contracting standpoint, we also need to see SOC 2 and the DPA — specifically clauses around sub processors, data residency, and liability caps.
00:01:28 Jonas Reed: we'll share the SOC 2 report and a standard DPA exemplar after the call.
00:01:34 Sara Lopez: good. pricing — our finance team wants committed capacity for predictable cost. what does committed look like and what are spike protections?
00:01:44 Maya Chen: typical pattern is reserved monthly GPU hours or reserved QPS, with burst pools. reserved gets you lower per-token rates and a contractual SLA. during bursts we can route to compatible variants; there are overflow policies for hosted capacity but you can opt into guaranteed burst in dedicated.
00:02:00 Raj Patel: SLA specifics — we need 99.9% availability and defined latency SLOs for our auth APIs, 95th and 99th p99 numbers. can you commit to measurable SLOs?
00:02:10 Ethan Park: yes, we publish per-model and per-route latency profiles. SLA language can include uptime and latency target bands, with credits for miss. we should pull the detailed SLA appendix into the MSA.
00:02:21 Noel? [brief crosstalk]
00:02:27 Hannah Chu: does Redwood support customer-managed keys in KMS across the board? specifically AWS KMS with HSM backed keys?
00:02:34 Ethan Park: yes. customer KMS is supported for private and dedicated deployments. for hosted we support envelope encryption where customer KMS keys encrypt the data keys — HSM-backed CMKs are supported but we'd need to map the keystore integration.
00:02:47 Raj Patel: And proof of key custody — do you provide attestation or key access logs?
00:02:51 Jonas Reed: we can surface key usage logs and we integrate with CloudTrail in typical cloud deployments; for private/on-prem you control the keys so key access is within your environment.
00:03:03 Sara Lopez: can you describe how you reduce PCI scope? tokenization, redaction — what's recommended?
00:03:10 Ethan Park: recommended is tokenize PANs before hitting our stack. alternate approach is cardholder data never leaves your token vault and only tokens are passed. Redwood has prefix caching and KV cache but that doesn't store raw PANs if customer requests no persistence.
00:03:26 Emily Tan: Emily here - legally we need a representation that raw PANs will never be stored or logged. is that in the DPA?
00:03:33 Maya Chen: we can add a DPA clause and an operational control - an explicit config flag that disables any input retention and redaction workflows, along with audit proof. we'll propose wording.
00:03:44 Raj Patel: auditability — in an incident we need packet-level traces for a 1 week window and user-level logs for 18 months. can Redwood export or stream logs to our SIEM?
00:03:55 Ethan Park: yes — log forwarding to customer SIEM via syslog or CloudWatch/BigQuery exports is supported. retention policy would live on customer side, but we can retain short-term traces for debugging during SLA windows.
00:04:07 Noah Rivers: latency testing — our auth path budget is 120ms end-to-end for LLM step. can Redwood hit p95 within 70ms for a 256 token prompt?
00:04:17 Ethan Park: typical hosted gen for 256 tokens is more like 150ms p95 on optimized model flavors, but for strict 70ms you'd likely need dedicated, optimized kernels, and some edge routing. we should run a benchmark with representative prompts and your network topology to confirm.
00:04:34 Sara Lopez: ok we want a pilot to validate. what are the deliverables from Redwood for that pilot?
00:04:40 Maya Chen: pilot deliverables: benchmark report (latency p50/p95/p99, throughput at X QPS), architecture runbook, security checklist, added SLA appendix draft, and a price proposal for committed tier if you want to convert to dedicated.
00:04:53 Emily Tan: on the MSA, liability caps are a sticking point. our legal wants carve-outs for gross negligence and forensic costs.
00:05:01 Maya Chen: understood; we can take standard enterprise-level carve-outs and our legal team will review redlines.
00:05:07 Raj Patel: encryption in transit — TLS? mTLS? we require mutual TLS for service-to-service in production.
00:05:13 Ethan Park: mTLS is supported for dedicated and VPC peered setups; hosted API supports TLS with token auth, and we can also set up customer-managed ingress proxies for mTLS.
00:05:25 Hannah Chu: any special controls for model hallucination that could leak sensitive data? we've heard models sometimes reconstruct training data.
00:05:33 Ethan Park: Redwood Optimize has quality monitoring and regression alerts; for sensitive workloads we recommend pinned model versions, deterministic sampling, and output filters/validators. also on dedicated/private you can run vetted open models that were not trained on your data.
00:05:48 Noah Rivers: do you support PCI scoped attestation or do customers still need their own QSA work?
00:05:55 Jonas Reed: customers still engage their QSA, but we supply artifacts (SOC 2, system diagrams, penetration test reports) that help reduce scope and evidence collection.
00:06:06 Sara Lopez: ok that helps. procurement-wise, target timeline is end of May to have a commercial agreement in place. finance needs numbers by next week.
00:06:15 Maya Chen: we'll send a pricing band and pilot SOW by Wednesday.
00:06:20 Emily Tan: legal needs the DPA exemplar sooner. can you share now?
00:06:24 Jonas Reed: yes, linking the DPA after the call - that will be a standard exemplar with notes.
00:06:30 Raj Patel: one more — do you perform vulnerability scanning and quarterly pen tests?
00:06:35 Ethan Park: yes, regular internal and third-party pen tests annually; we can provide recent reports under NDA. we also do dependency scanning and container hardening.
00:06:46 Sara Lopez: fine. any competitors you're typically compared to?
00:06:50 Maya Chen: most enterprise customers ask about OpenAI and Anthropic for model capabilities, and cloud native vendors like GCP Vertex for managed endpoints; Redwood differentiators are the multi-deployment model and cost/performance controls.
00:07:03 Emily Tan: do you have references in payments?
00:07:06 Maya Chen: we have two anonymized payments references we can share that have gone through dedicated deployments; we'll include condensed reference sheets.
00:07:15 Hannah Chu: network detail — we will need a diagram and exact egress IPs for firewall rules.
00:07:20 Ethan Park: noted — we'll send egress ranges for the dedicated region and VPC peering steps.
00:07:27 Sara Lopez: ok next steps recap?
00:07:30 Maya Chen: I'll recap: send security packet + SOC2, pricing bands and pilot SOW, run benchmark (Ethan), DPA exemplar and wait for Emily's redlines.
00:07:40 Emily Tan: timeline — I aim to have redlines in 1 week.
00:07:44 Jonas Reed: action items noted.

00:08:00 [Longer technical dig in — 40 minute deep dive follows — timestamps skip ahead to key moments to reflect flow]
00:08:15 Ethan Park: (screen share described) here's a simplified flow: client -> token vault -> Redwood ingress -> model runtime -> Redwood egress. token vault retains PAN, Redwood only sees tokens. if customer insists, we can run token resolution inside your VPC which keeps PAN fully in your network.
00:09:05 Raj Patel: can we see the template network diagram?
00:09:10 Ethan Park: yes uploaded link: https://redwood.company/security/finova-net-diagram (link placeholder). note in transcribed text sometimes links are truncated.
00:10:40 Noah Rivers: about data residency — we need EU-only processing for EU cardholders. is that simply region pinning?
00:10:48 Maya Chen: yes, region pinning plus route enforcement. for Hosted we can pin to EU regions and block cross-region fallback, or run a Private EU deployment. we'll document region commit terms in the DPA appendix.
00:12:12 Sara Lopez: billing model question — if we commit to reserved capacity and our usage drops, what flexibility is there?
00:12:20 Maya Chen: commitments are typically 12 months with quarterly true-ups. we can build in a step-down clause or buffer if you show historic seasonality. we'll draft acceptable bands.
00:13:30 Hannah Chu: regarding CI/CD, do you provide docker images for on-prem?
00:13:36 Ethan Park: yes, there's an on-prem package and container images. for air-gapped installs we have an install iso and offline key provisioning.
00:14:10 Raj Patel: phone a bit — sorry. {laughs} one more question on forensic exports — file formats?
00:14:16 Ethan Park: we export logs as JSONL and can stream to your SIEM via syslog or S3 export with server-side encryption.
00:15:05 Emily Tan: legal clause around sub processors — we need a list and 30-day notice for changes. can you do that?
00:15:12 Jonas Reed: yes we publish sub processor list and commit to notice.
00:16:00 Sara Lopez: ok, we will need a non-prod pilot environment and a production plan. what's the cost for a short 2-week pilot?
00:16:08 Maya Chen: pilots are often low-cost: we can offer a scoped pilot for a small flat fee to cover reserved capacity for the run and validation work; then a conversion credit if you proceed to a commit. I'll include numbers in the SOW.
00:16:20 Noah Rivers: do you do tokenization as a managed service?
00:16:24 Ethan Park: we don't manage customer PAN token vaults, but we can provide a reference implementation and help with integration in professional services.
00:17:01 Raj Patel: are there certifications for key management? like FIPS 140-2 HSM?
00:17:05 Ethan Park: our partners support FIPS HSM-backed CMKs, yes. for private on-prem we can integrate with your HSM.
00:18:40 Maya Chen: quick note on regression alerts — Redwood Optimize can run continuous evals against production prompts to watch for quality drift; for payments you can flag false positives/negatives on auth decisions.
00:19:02 Hannah Chu: curious about model updates — how do you handle forced model upgrades?
00:19:07 Ethan Park: customers pin model versions and we support canary rollouts; forced upgrades are rare and contractual via change notice.
00:20:30 Emily Tan: on indemnity and liability — can Redwood accept limited carve-outs related to data breaches if we follow recommended configs?
00:20:37 Maya Chen: we'd need legal to trade on that and map the security controls; it's negotiable in MSA with appropriate controls in place.
00:22:50 Sara Lopez: procurement wants to know the exact SLA credit formula. can we get the SLA appendix?
00:22:56 Jonas Reed: yes, we'll attach the SLA appendix which includes uptime calculations, latency SLOs, and credit bands.
00:25:10 Ethan Park: (walkthrough of benchmark plan) we'll run three load tiers: light/medium/heavy, measure p50/p95/p99, and test an overflow scenario. we'll also test the 70ms p95 target to see if dedicated plus edge routing is required.
00:27:40 Noah Rivers: ok that's perfect. any blockers for us to start?
00:27:46 Maya Chen: main blockers: Emily's DPA redlines and Hannah's network diagram + egress firewall list. once we have those we'll schedule the benchmark.
00:28:05 Emily Tan: will do.
00:28:12 Sara Lopez: wrap-up — we need price numbers by next Wednesday.
00:28:18 Maya Chen: we'll do that.
00:28:23 [Meeting winds down — light chat about travel and references]
00:31:00 Maya Chen: thanks everyone. we'll follow up with links and the SOW.
00:31:06 Sara Lopez: thanks.
00:31:12 Raj Patel: thanks all.
00:31:18 [Call ends at 15:48 PT — transcript truncated for brevity]
